LESSON: JEWELLERY AND ORNAMENTATION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: FINE ARTS
Strand: Indigenous Crafts (3D Art)
Topic 3.4: Jewellery and Ornamentation
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Jewellery and Ornamentation, part of Indigenous Crafts (3D Art) in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 FINE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How does jewellery and ornamentation contribute to environmental conservation?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Jewellery and Ornamentation together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner explores the environment, collects and prepares materials

for leatherwork and jewellery while producing various functional and decorative items.

● Communication as the learner;

- seeks information and offers support while sourcing, preparing, using materials and sharing what they have

learnt with others.

- pays attention to the person speaking, takes turns in conversation during critique of own and others’ mixed- media artworks.

● Collaboration: as the learner amicably works together with peers, appreciates efforts of others while sourcing

materials for leatherwork and jewellery.

Values:
● Respect: as the learner appreciates diverse opinions and values human dignity during critique sessions.

● Social justice: as learners appreciate boundaries and permission while sourcing and preparing materials for jewellery and

ornaments

Suggested Learning Resources:

Internet, ICT devices, video demonstrations on the process of creating jewellery and ornaments, samples of

jewellery and ornaments, needles, cutting tools, threads, wires, found or recyclable objects, adapted digital devices,

page turners, book holders, universal cuffs, multipurpose communication board text-to-speech software, footboard,

adapted cutting tools, unscented heat dyes, adapted iron boxes

Other Related Service Providers:

Resource person, Speech Therapist , Learner support assistance, Occupational Therapist, Physiotherapist,
